chapter_note: This chapter is dominated by hagiographic/pastoral discourse in Mani’s first-person voice to the community (elect, charity, love/obedience), wrapped in a formulaic opening. The sun-ray analogy functions as exhortation and self-identification rather than impersonal, systematic cosmological mapping. No extractable pre-compilation core teaching layer is securely present.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic dialogue/frame opener: ‘Once again he speaks… sits in the midst of the congregation’—editorial hagiographic apparatus.

Didactic exhortation (‘Note how…’) using a natural analogy about the sun; no numbered structures or cosmological mechanics, and it serves as setup for community-directed application rather than standalone systematic teaching.

First-person self-identification (‘this is also what I am like’) with explicit institutional categories (‘children… righteous elect… believed in me’) and promise to gather believers; this reads as community address rather than impersonal pre-compilation cosmology.

Explicit ethical/institutional exhortation (love the elect, charity, mixing with them) and salvific promise; classic pastoral layer. The cosmological phrase ‘black universe’ is used as moral-eschatological rhetoric, not systematic exposition.
